note: Viewing places near the launch sites, each fact with its source (docs/GOWATCH_SOURCES.md). Distances are worked out by the build from each place to the launch's pad, straight line.

places.name: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex (Main Visitor Complex, North Atlantis Lawn)
places.parking: Paid, collected before the parking plaza: automobiles $15, motorcycles $5, oversized vehicles/motor homes/RVs $20, group tour buses free (KSC FAQ). Lot size not stated.
places.fees: Daily admission required (price not read for this report). Launch viewing is offered for some launches only; the Gantry is sold in addition to daily admission. Launch ticket prices not stated on the pages read.
places.closures: FAQ header: 9 AM to 5 PM; NASA: opens at 9 a.m. Viewing availability depends on the launch window, pad, Visitor Complex operations, Range Safety and NASA approval, and expected interest (KSC viewing page).
places.arrive: No time given. NASA: arrive early on launch day; buy tickets online and show them on your phone.
places.restrooms: not stated on the viewing page
places.notes: Main Visitor Complex: guests see the rocket once it clears the tree line; bleacher and lawn seating. Accessibility (KSC FAQ): Guest Accessibility Pass at the Information center; wheelchair $10 plus tax per day; electric convenience vehicle $30 plus tax; service dogs welcome. Package guests ride Visitor Complex buses through NASA gates; no self driving.

places.name: Playalinda Beach, Canaveral National Seashore
places.parking: During launches parking only in the beach parking lots (NPS). Size not stated. When the park fills it restricts entry for a period; no number given.
places.fees: Private vehicle $25 (7 days); motorcycle $20; per person (hiker, bicyclist, pedestrian) $15; under 16 free; park annual pass $45; America the Beautiful passes accepted. No cash: cards and touchless only (NPS fees page, updated Jan 1, 2026).
places.closures: Launch viewing only during operating hours: summer launches 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM, winter 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM (NPS). During launches: Playalinda District vistas close; the beach at lot 1 closes for a quarter mile south to the KSC boundary; Playalinda Beach Road closes between the entry gate and lot 1 thirty minutes before launch, reopening right after a successful launch or confirmed cancellation; NASA may close NASA owned parts without notice (NPS). One LC-39A launch (2021): everything from parking area 13 south to the Playalinda Road Gate closed (NPS). Artemis II from LC-39B (2026): hours 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. until launch, lots 1 to 3 closed, no foot traffic south of lot 4, beach road vistas closed while the rocket was on the pad (NPS).
places.arrive: NPS: 'a few hours early if possible'.
places.restrooms: not stated on the launch page (it says there are no showers).
places.notes: NPS: bring food, water, sunscreen, beach chairs, a full gas tank and a hat. Closest public beach to LC-39A/39B, and the most closure prone.

places.name: Jetty Park, Port Canaveral
places.parking: Day pass or annual pass required to park. Artemis II: day passes sold out in advance; pre purchased day pass holders guaranteed entry (not re entry); annual passholders not guaranteed; the park closes at 100% vehicle capacity (Port Canaveral, Mar 30, 2026). Size not stated. No other public parking on Port property that day; no parking or viewing on SR 401, George King Blvd or Port property.
places.fees: Day pass price not stated in the official article read (Florida Today: parking charges collected). Walk ins and bicyclists admitted until capacity.
places.closures: Artemis II day: 7 a.m. to 9 p.m., until capacity (Port Canaveral). Normal hours not read (the Port's recreation FAQ URL returned 404).
places.arrive: Port Canaveral: allow extra driving time (no time).
places.notes: Drones strictly prohibited (Port Canaveral). After launch deputies routed departing cars onto Shorewood Drive toward N. Atlantic Blvd; electronic signs on SR 528, A1A and Port roads show restrictions and when parking is full. 400 Jetty Park Road (Florida Today).
